passages.original: Unde Herodes Cæsari querelam detulit: sed vindictam imperatam a Caesare indignatio Dei sustulit. Nam in ipso apparatu belli, Cæsaris mors nuntiata. idque a Judæis aestimatum comperimus et creditum (auctore Josepho adversum se tdoneo) quod non fraude hominum, sed Dei commotione Herodes exercitum amiserit etjustequidem propter vindictam Joannis Baptistae viri justi qui dixerat ei: Non licet tibi fralri, uxorem habere (Marc.
passages.english: So Herod brought a complaint to Caesar; but the vengeance that Caesar ordered was taken away by the indignation of God. For in the very preparation of the war, Caesar's death was announced. And we find that the Jews judged and believed (on the authority of Josephus, a competent witness against them) that Herod lost his army not through the deceit of men but through the stirring of God, and justly indeed, as vengeance for John the Baptist, a just man, who had said to him: "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife" (Mark
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'tdoneo' read as 'idoneo'; 'etjustequidem' as 'et juste quidem'; 'fralri' as 'fratri'. The scripture reference continues in the following passage (Mark 6:18). 'adversum se idoneo' is taken as 'a witness competent [even] against them [the Jews]'.

passages.original: Ad hæc Josephus refert : Et quis velit esse tantæ mortis superstes? Quis eligat neri haeres doloris ? Quis animam suam nolit ex ipso corpore mortis, si ticcat, absolvi ? ced non licet solvere, nisi ei qui ligaverit.
passages.english: To this Josephus replies: "And who would wish to survive so great a death? Who would choose to become the heir of [such] grief? Who would not want his soul to be released from this very body of death, if it were permitted? But it is not permitted to loose [it], except for him who bound [it]."
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'neri' read as 'fieri'; 'ticcat' as 'liceat'; 'ced' as 'sed'.
